explained.summary: Whenever something makes a strong impression on you, break it down: what kind of thing it is, what it’s made of, what it’s for, and how long it will last. Most strong reactions shrink once you see a thing in parts and remember that it’s temporary.
explained.today: A glowing review of a gadget you suddenly need, or a scary headline, can be taken apart the same way. It’s plastic and metal, it does one job, and it’ll be out of date in two years. The headline is words chosen to grab you, and next week it will be forgotten.
